does: Pulls soft herb leaves apart with the fingers instead of cutting them, just before they are used, so that the edges stay green and the leaves keep their scent.

intro.what: Soft herbs are torn by hand right before they go into a dish.
intro.why: Tearing bruises soft leaves less than a blunt knife and keeps them fresh and fragrant.

how: Wait until the dish is nearly ready.
Pick the leaves from the stems and tear them into pieces with your fingers.
Add them straight away, off the heat or at the very end.

cues.text: A strong, fresh scent as the leaves tear.
Bright green leaves with clean edges, not dark and bruised.

mistakes.mistake: Chopping soft leaves long before they are needed, so that they turn black.
mistakes.fix: Tear them just before they go in.

mistakes.mistake: Cooking the torn leaves for a long time, so that their scent is lost.
mistakes.fix: Add them at the end or off the heat.

quiz.question: Why tear soft herbs by hand?
choices: To bruise them as much as possible.
To keep their edges green and their scent fresh.
quiz.because: Tearing does less damage than a blunt knife.

quiz.question: When should you tear the leaves?
quiz.because: Torn leaves darken as they wait.

quiz.question: How should the torn leaves look?
quiz.because: Fresh green leaves show they were not bruised.

quiz.question: The basil turned black and lost its smell. What would you change next time?
choices: Tear it earlier and cook it longer.
Tear it at the last moment and add it at the end.
quiz.because: Late tearing and little heat keep basil fresh.
